content:
The test image shows a soybean seedling lying on soil with:
- Yellowed/tan cotyledons that appear collapsed and wilted
- Brown, rotted hypocotyl at/near soil line
- The seedling has "damped off" — fallen over at the soil line
- Soft rot appearance rather than firm/dry lesions

This matches **Pythium_damping_off** closely:
- Water-soaked lesions on hypocotyl/cotyledons developing into brown soft rot
- Seedling collapsed at soil line
- The reference collage shows nearly identical presentation — green-to-yellow cotyledons with rotted brown hypocotyls lying on wet soil

Distinguishing from Rhizoctonia (firm, dry, reddish-brown lesions — not soft rot) and Phytophthora (dark brown lesion extending upward from taproot on more developed plants).
